title: distinguishable states
rule: Button states (enabled, disabled, hover, focus, pressed) must be visually distinguishable from each other.
pass_when: Enabled, disabled, hover, focus, and pressed are visually distinguishable from each other.
fail_when: Any two of those states look the same.
overview: Each button state—enabled, disabled, hover, focus, pressed—looks different.
apply_when: Styling interactive buttons that change with pointer and keyboard.
not_when: Static non-interactive badges or plain text that never change state.
agent_hint: Make enabled, disabled, hover, focus, and pressed visually distinct.
description: A button only communicates interaction if its states are easy to tell apart. Enabled, disabled, hover, focus, and pressed must each have a distinct visual treatment so people can see affordance, focus, and acceptance of input. Collapse any two of those looks and the control becomes ambiguous. Apply this to real buttons; decorative chips that never receive interaction are out of scope.
